sections.title: Economic channel · Inflation and wages
sections.body: Inflation and wages inform purchasing power, profit margins and the policy outlook. Model assumption: The currency model assumes higher inflation increases tightening pressure. Index and crypto models apply the discount-rate channel. Conditions: Supply shocks, stagflation and credibility concerns can reverse the currency response. High inflation is not automatically risk-on.

sections.title: Economic channel · Employment
sections.body: Employment and unemployment inform income, demand and resource slack. Model assumption: Stronger employment supports currency and earnings channels; unemployment and claims use inverse direction. Conditions: Strong jobs can also increase expected interest rates. Revisions, labour-force participation and the business cycle matter.

sections.title: Economic channel · Growth and activity
sections.body: Output and demand influence earnings, imports and industrial commodity consumption. Model assumption: Improving activity supports the currency and index earnings channels; commodity effects depend on the mapped consuming economy. Conditions: A rising PMI below 50 is improvement, not necessarily expansion. Annual and quarterly series cannot be treated as interchangeable.

sections.title: Economic channel · Energy inventories
sections.body: Inventory changes reflect the balance between production, imports and consumption. Model assumption: Inventory draws support the oil demand/supply channel; builds weigh on it. Conditions: Seasonality, refinery maintenance, exports and expectations can change the interpretation. The direction alone is not a forecast.

methodology.name: Monetary policy
methodology.mechanism: Policy rates influence financing costs, asset discount rates and relative currency returns.
methodology.mapping: Higher policy-rate changes support the currency channel; they weigh on equity, crypto and precious-metal discount-rate channels.
methodology.limit: Markets react to expected future policy and surprises. A rate hike already priced in can coincide with a weaker currency.

methodology.name: Inflation and wages
methodology.mechanism: Inflation and wages inform purchasing power, profit margins and the policy outlook.
methodology.mapping: The currency model assumes higher inflation increases tightening pressure. Index and crypto models apply the discount-rate channel.
methodology.limit: Supply shocks, stagflation and credibility concerns can reverse the currency response. High inflation is not automatically risk-on.

methodology.name: Employment
methodology.mechanism: Employment and unemployment inform income, demand and resource slack.
methodology.mapping: Stronger employment supports currency and earnings channels; unemployment and claims use inverse direction.
methodology.limit: Strong jobs can also increase expected interest rates. Revisions, labour-force participation and the business cycle matter.

methodology.name: Growth and activity
methodology.mechanism: Output and demand influence earnings, imports and industrial commodity consumption.
methodology.mapping: Improving activity supports the currency and index earnings channels; commodity effects depend on the mapped consuming economy.
methodology.limit: A rising PMI below 50 is improvement, not necessarily expansion. Annual and quarterly series cannot be treated as interchangeable.

methodology.name: External balance
methodology.mechanism: Trade flows and external financing affect demand for currencies.
methodology.mapping: Only explicitly classified releases are used; a trade-balance improvement is a conditional currency support.
methodology.limit: Imports can rise because domestic demand is strong. Reserve changes and managed exchange rates do not have a universal trading sign.

methodology.name: Energy inventories
methodology.mechanism: Inventory changes reflect the balance between production, imports and consumption.
methodology.mapping: Inventory draws support the oil demand/supply channel; builds weigh on it.
methodology.limit: Seasonality, refinery maintenance, exports and expectations can change the interpretation. The direction alone is not a forecast.

methodology.name: Reported futures positioning
methodology.mechanism: COT measures positions in specified futures markets and trader categories.
methodology.mapping: Net contracts divided by open interest is a positioning input. One family and contract avoid duplicate votes.
methodology.limit: Positions are lagged holdings, not certain intentions. Extreme positioning is not an automatic reversal signal; non-reportable does not mean retail.

methodology.name: Crypto network and liquidity
methodology.mechanism: Activity, issuance and stablecoin balances describe usage, supply pressure and chain liquidity.
methodology.mapping: Complete 7/30-day windows create separate network, supply and liquidity factors, then blend with macro and direct positioning.
methodology.limit: Bots, congestion and token design break simple usage-to-price relationships. Unlocks, value capture and ETF flows are incomplete.
